title: orbit project configuration (ui-tests/project.json)
description: The consuming project's answers to what the engine cannot know: where the app is, how to read the database, which script opens a signed-in browser, which browser it opens, which hosts mean an identity provider is asking for credentials, where the frontend checkout is. Relative paths resolve against the project root (the parent of ui-tests/); `~` and `${ENV}` expand; an entry whose ${ENV} is unset is dropped. ORBIT_ORIGIN, ORBIT_RUN_DIR, ORBIT_FRONTEND_ROOT, ORBIT_CHANNEL and ORBIT_ENV override their fields per run (the older PT_ names are still read).

name.description: Short project name; the default run directory is <tmpdir>/pw-<name>.

origin.description: The app under test. A goto step's path is appended to it.

runDir.description: Where the launcher writes .playwright/cli.config.json — the directory playwright-cli finds its session through. Default <tmpdir>/pw-<name>.

launcher.description: Script that opens a signed-in browser and prints `run directory : <dir>` and `target        : <url>` lines. run-awake spawns it with --channel/--headed|--headless/--env/--profile and, per identity, --run-dir.

reports.description: Directory for the generated HTML reports — the one artefact meant for a person rather than for the engine. A run's report is filed under <screen>/<case>/, a page about many runs under _screens/, _plans/, _sessions/ or _investigations/, and each is a single self-contained file with every screenshot base64-embedded. Defaults to <store>/reports/, in the machine store and never in the checkout: a committed report publishes the pictures of whatever tenant the run drove. A path inside the checkout is copied into the store as well.

retention.description: How many evidence directories to keep per case in the machine store; the newest failure is always kept. 0 keeps everything. Evidence is disposable once its report exists, because the report embeds every picture it shows.

command.description: Command that runs a read-only query given as its LAST argument and prints pipe-separated rows under a dashed line. Credentials stay with this tool, never here.

timeoutSec.description: Seconds one sql.command call may take before it is killed (default 120, ORBIT_DB_TIMEOUT). A query that never answers is BLOCKED, not a product failure.

signIn.description: How to tell that the browser is parked on a sign-in page instead of in the app — a per-product fact, since the host belongs to your identity provider.

hosts.description: Host fragments that mean "an identity provider is asking for credentials", e.g. ["login.microsoftonline.com"] or ["accounts.google.com"] or your own SSO host. A session on one of these is REFUSED with "finish signing in" instead of timing out mid-case. Empty: no host is ever treated as a sign-in page.

launch.description: Defaults run-awake passes to the launcher; ORBIT_CHANNEL and ORBIT_ENV override them per run.

channel.description: Browser channel the launcher should open, e.g. chromium, chrome, msedge. Default chromium.

env.description: Which deployment the launcher should point at, passed as --env. Default test.

roots.description: Candidate checkouts of the frontend, first existing wins; `git rev-parse` there is the fe_commit a live run is stamped with.

srcDir.description: Sub-directory of a root that `src` references in the map are relative to, e.g. app/src.

identity.description: Which of the tokens a signed-in profile holds speaks for THIS app, and what its provider calls the claims. A profile holds several -- the app's id token carries the roles, a token for some other API carries none -- and picking the wrong one decides whose authority a permission case believes it observed. Needed only where a session holds more than one: with a single token the engine uses it, with several and nothing declared it REFUSES and names them rather than guessing.

audience.description: The `aud` claim of the app's own token, e.g. "api://my-app". The one key most projects need.

issuer.description: The `iss` claim, when audience alone still matches more than one token.

rolesClaim.description: The claim carrying the role list, if your provider does not call it `roles`.

upnClaim.description: The claim carrying the user's name, if your provider does not call it `upn`.
